title: Nuclear Caucus
raw_text:
Nuclear Energy Caucus and Three Mile Island
Rep. Tom Mehaffie serves as a co-chair on the bipartisan, bicameral Nuclear Energy Caucus within the Pennsylvania General Assembly. In September 2024, Constellation Energy announced its intention to resume production at the Three Mile Island plant in Dauphin County.
Rep. Mehaffie authored a guest editorial about the announcement for PennLive.com.
You can read it here.
He sought input from the community about the plant and wrote a guest editorial for the Hummelstown Sun about that feedback.
You can read it here.
Additionally, the community response was captured in a series of videos you can watch at the bottom of this page.
Mehaffie’s legislation in 2022 led to a Joint State Government Commission report about the benefits of nuclear energy and the development of small modular reactors.
You can read that report here.
Page 17 references the 2019 closure of Three Mile Island, which is on track to reopen as the Crane Clean Energy Center in 2027.
The representative introduced legislation increasing fees paid to the state by nuclear plant operators. You can read more about that legislation
here.
If you are a resident of the 106th District,
use this form
to ask questions or provide feedback about the Nuclear Energy Caucus.
Videos:
Nuclear Plant Tour
Rep. Tom Mehaffie joined two House committees on a tour of the Crane Clean Energy Center in October 2025.
Crane Clean Energy Center
Rep. Tom Mehaffie spoke at the Crane Clean Energy Center in June 2025.
Data Centers’ Impact on Power Grid
In March 2025, Rep. Tom Mehaffie questioned Public Utility Commission Chairman Stephen Defrank about how data centers and artificial intelligence will place additional demands on the 13-state power grid.
TMI Stories: Union Jobs
Rob Bair from the PA State Building & Construction Trades Council anticipates plentiful, well-paying jobs at Three Mile Island as the plant is brought back online.
TMI Stories: Business Climate
Dave Kitner from Roberto’s Pizza in Middletown experienced a drop-off in business when Three Mile Island shut down production in 2019. He is eager for its return.
TMI Stories: Charities
Lower Dauphin Communities That Care received financial contributions from the owners of Three Mile Island prior to the plant being taken offline in 2019. The charitable giving made the nonprofit organization’s Books on Board (Bookmobile) program possible. Constellation Energy has committed to $1 million in philanthropy over five years as the plant resumes production.
TMI Stories: Fire Company
Londonderry Fire Chief Bart Shellenhamer works with the Nuclear Regulatory Commission to ensure yearly training requirements are met for any potential emergency response to Three Mile Island. He described partnering closely with the plant’s staff and being appreciative of past financial contributions, some of which allowed for loan payments on the firehouse’s expansion.
TMI Stories: Training Programs
Heat & Frost Insulators Local 23 hosts training and apprenticeship programs in Grantville. Students have had to travel farther since 2019 to meet their training requirements in commercial and industrial settings.
TMI Stories: Restart Overview
Dave Marcheskie from Constellation Energy addresses resumed production on Three Mile Island, which will be rebranded as the Crane Clean Energy Center.

Welcome to the I-83 Capital Beltway Project
The Harrisburg Capital Beltway encircles the City of Harrisburg, which is the State Capital of Pennsylvania, and surrounding municipalities. The Beltway includes a section of Interstate 81 (I-81), a section of Interstate 83 (I-83), and Route 581, and is a limited-access facility. The Capital Beltway is vital to the economy of the Harrisburg region, and is an important hub in the transportation network of the northeastern United States. This website focuses on the I-83 section of the Beltway, which extends from a junction with I-81 northeast of Harrisburg to the interchange with Route 581 to the south of Harrisburg. An I-83 Master Plan was prepared by the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT) in 2003 for this section of the Capital Beltway to identify, plan, and program future transportation improvement projects.
The I-83 Capital Beltway has three major issues that the projects will address:
Worsening roadway conditions – Most of the pavement in the I-83 corridor is over 50 years old and has been repeatedly patched and overlaid while the base pavement continues to age.
High traffic volumes and congestion – The existing traffic and the traffic predicted to use the roadway in the future, are more than the roadway can effectively carry.
Safety – The roadway was designed more than 50 years ago and does not include the modern safety features needed for roadways that have many vehicles traveling at high speeds.
What's new?
The I-83 East Shore Section 3 (ESS3) – PennDOT opened bids for the second construction contract (Contract 2) and notice to proceed is expected to be given this fall. For more information and status of this project, view the
I-83 East Shore Section 3 project page.

title: #TheKiss4PA
raw_text:
#TheKiss4PA
Starting in 2021, Rep. Tom Mehaffie (R-Dauphin) has introduced legislation that would name Hershey’s Kisses the state candy of Pennsylvania. He drafted the bills in partnership with teenagers from Council Rock School District.
The bill would add Hershey’s Kisses to the list of state symbols, which includes mountain laurel as the state flower, white-tailed deer as the state animal, and, as of 2019, the Eastern hellbender as the state amphibian.
A class at Newtown Middle School started the project to seek designation for Hershey’s Kisses while learning about civics. Those students are now high-schoolers, but they have continued to advocate for the project and created
thekiss4pa.org
to promote it.

title: Bill Respecting Law Enforcement Families Passes House, Mehaffie Says
raw_text:
Bill Respecting Law Enforcement Families Passes House, Mehaffie Says
September 30, 2026
HARRISBURG – Legislation seeking to ensure the dependents of fallen police officers continue to have health insurance passed the House of Representatives today on a unanimous vote, according to the bill’s sponsor, Rep. Tom Mehaffie (R-Dauphin).
“If it becomes law,
House Bill 911
would ensure that the families of fallen officers have continued access to health care while providing greater financial security and peace of mind during an incredibly difficult time,” Mehaffie said.
Mehaffie said he was inspired to introduce the legislation after speaking with the widow of a local police officer who died in the line of duty. During their conversations, Jackie Henry described the challenges and uncertainty she faced regarding health insurance coverage following her husband’s death.
“When a law enforcement officer makes the ultimate sacrifice, his or her family’s protection shouldn’t depend on the municipality they served. House Bill 911 is about keeping a promise to the families who kept theirs,” Henry said. “I’m deeply grateful to Rep. Mehaffie and everyone who has worked together to move this legislation forward so that no surviving spouse or child has to face the uncertainty my family, and so many others before ours, experienced.”
House Bill 911 would provide insurance to the surviving spouse for his or her lifetime, and children would be covered until age 26. The proposal mirrors the benefits already available to Pennsylvania State Police families experiencing line-of-duty deaths.
Mehaffie emphasized that his conversations with Derry Township Officer Michael L. Henry Jr.’s family made it clear that changes are needed.
“Families who have already endured the profound loss of a loved one should not have to face additional financial or health insurance uncertainty during their time of grief,” he said. “This legislation honors the commitment officers make to our communities.”
House Bill 911 goes to the Senate for its consideration.

title: Kim, Mehaffie to Host Senior Fraud Prevention Event
raw_text:
Kim, Mehaffie to Host Senior Fraud Prevention Event
September 21, 2026
HARRISBURG – Sen. Patty Kim (D-Dauphin) and Rep. Tom Mehaffie (R-Dauphin) are joining to host a senior fraud and scam prevention event Friday, Sept. 25.
Older adults and their caregivers are invited to attend the free event from 9 a.m. to noon at DaySpring Ministries, 1600 Spring Garden Drive, Middletown.
Personnel from the Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General and Mid Penn Bank will present information about ways consumers can protect themselves from common scams, identity theft and fraud.
“In today’s world it’s easier than ever for our seniors to fall victim to scams that rob them of their money, their identity, and, above all else, their dignity,” Kim said. “It’s a scary reality, but we can’t just bury our heads in the sand. We want to not only make seniors aware of these scams but also give them the knowledge and tools to protect themselves and their assets.”
“Just last week, I heard from a woman who had nearly fallen victim to a pervasive telephone scam,” Mehaffie said. “Modern technology is emboldening fraudsters to prey on so many people. My hope is this event gives Dauphin County residents the tools and knowledge to safeguard themselves.”
No pre-registration is required to attend. Those with questions are invited to call 717-534-1323.

title: Mehaffie, Kim Announce State Gaming Grants for Municipalities
raw_text:
Mehaffie, Kim Announce State Gaming Grants for Municipalities
September 15, 2026
HARRISBURG – Parks and sidewalks are among the projects that Dauphin County municipalities will be undertaking courtesy of Local Share Account (LSA) grants awarded today, according to Rep. Tom Mehaffie (R-Dauphin) and Sen. Patty Kim (D-Dauphin).
More than $1.1 million in grants awarded include:
•	Lower Swatara Township, $475,000 for a new basketball court and playground equipment in Greenfield Park.
•	Middletown Borough, $497,000 to replace deteriorating sidewalks and install handicapped-accessible curbs on several streets.
•	Royalton Borough, $89,500 to address flooding between Canal Street and Water Street.
•	Royalton Borough, $66,000 to purchase a police vehicle to replace one destroyed at an emergency scene.
“Our municipal leaders are doing more with less every day. Helping them with these initiatives will provide even more services within their communities and ultimately save local taxpayers money,” Mehaffie said.
“This round of state investments demonstrates just how important it is for us to come together to bring meaningful results to our constituents. I’m proud to work alongside my colleagues in the House to secure this funding, and I’m especially proud to see it going to our first responders, municipalities, nonprofits and other essential community organizations,” Kim said.
Additionally, Mehaffie advocated for a $995,058 grant for Harrisburg’s Zembo Shrine, of which he is a longtime member. Construction started almost 100 years on the building designed by architect Charles Howard Lloyd in a combination of Moorish revival and art deco styles. It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Funding will be used to replace a boiler and sections of the roof.
LSA grants are funded by state gaming revenue, not taxpayer dollars. The funding was approved by the Commonwealth Financing Authority (CFA). This is an independent agency that holds fiduciary responsibility over the funding of programs and investments in Pennsylvania’s economic growth.
